paper_metadata.title: Ultrastrong bicontinuous-nanostructured W-Cr alloy formed by discontinuous precipitation

evidence.quote: A dual-phase W-Cr refractory alloy was prepared via a processing route involving sintering, homogenization and discontinuous precipitation, exhibiting a bicontinuous nanostructure consisting of two nanoscale phases with identical crystal structures, while maintaining a microscale grain size.
following phase replacing in liquid Zn and cooling to room temperature, a W/Zn nanocomposite with 5 vol.% residual W-Cr structures at some of grain boundaries was prepared.
after phase replacing in liquid Cu at 1100 ◦C, significant coarsening occurred, resulting in an average W ligament size of 250 nm in the prepared W/Cu nanocomposite

Mixed powders of 34 at.% tungsten (W) and 66 at.% chromium (Cr) (purchased from Liaoning Zhongse Novel Material and Technology Co., Ltd) were fabricated by ball mill of high-purity W and Cr powders (99.9 wt.% purity, 40-50 μm particle size).

the mixed powders were sintered using a fast hot press sintering furnace (FHP-828, Haatn), with temperature rapidly increasing to 1400 ◦C at a heating rate as 100 ◦C/min, holding for 30 min, then cooling rapidly to room temperature. Throughout the sintering process, the vacuum was kept below 10−2 Pa and a constant pressure of 50 MPa was applied.
All sintered W-Cr specimens were subsequently homogenized at 1600 ◦C for 3 h and quenched using high-pressure Argon.

Following homogenization, the W-Cr alloys underwent discontinuous precipitation (DP) treatment by annealing at 1080 ◦C for 2 h under an Ar atmosphere, followed by quenching in water to obtain dual-phase nanostructures.
To produce coarsened dual-phase structures, a subset of the homogenized samples were annealed at 1200 ◦C for predetermined durations (2 h, 5 h and 24 h) prior to annealing at 1080 ◦C for 2 h.

other.medium: molten pure Zn in graphite crucible

evidence.quote: A DP-treated W-Cr specimen (1080 ◦C for 2 h) was cut into a 1.0 mm thick plate and immersed into molten pure Zn held at 700 ◦C for 6 h in a graphite crucible to replace the Cr phase with Zn.
The Zn phase was then replaced with Cu by immersing into molten pure Cu at 1100 ◦C for 10 min. After withdrawal from the liquid Cu and cooling to room temperature, a W/Cu nanocomposite was obtained.
the W34Cr66 alloy in this study is expected to form a single BCC phase at the homogenization temperature of 1600 ◦C, which is in consistent with the observed intragranular microstructure.
